ai.description: This slender viper reaches 60 cm. It is bright green with a pale venter and a distinct reddish-brown tail. Key features include a white postocular stripe and a single pair of enlarged internasals.
ai.identificationRemarks: The *Trimeresurus labialis* is uniquely distinguished by the presence of a distinct, narrow white or yellowish stripe running along the upper edge of its labial scales.
ai.habitat: The Island Pit Viper inhabits the tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of the Nicobar Islands, typically found in low-to-mid-altitude dense vegetation.
ai.behavior: The Island Pit Viper is primarily nocturnal, often positioning itself on low-hanging branches to ambush passing prey under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Trimeresurus labialis* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to live young. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with litters typically consisting of 3–7 neonates.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Trimeresurus labialis* is endemic to the Nicobar Islands in the Bay of Bengal, where it inhabits tropical forests from sea level to moderate elevations.
